title: When gratitude feels thin
issueStatement: The day may still contain mercy, but the heart has narrowed itself around what is missing, delayed, or undeservedly difficult.
centralInsight: Gurbani restores gratitude by returning the soul to gift, mercy, and Naam rather than asking for a performance of positivity.
practicalReflection: Gratitude is not a bright mood pasted over pain. It is truthful recognition that you are still being carried, guided, and given more than you can manufacture for yourself.
actionPrompt: Name one mercy beneath the surface event today, and stay with it long enough for entitlement to loosen.
searchTerms: learning a steadier way with gratitude

source.shortMeaning: Suffering is the medicine, and pleasure the disease, because where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God; i can do nothing. Even if I try, nothing happens
source.lifeApplication: Let one received thing become a place of praise instead of entitlement. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: The line makes gratitude possible even where life feels costly. Mercy is not reduced to pleasant circumstances; it is present in the healing the soul would otherwise refuse.

source.shortMeaning: You took pity on me, and blessed me with Your Mercy, and I have met the True Guru, my Friend; i have not appreciated what You have done for me, Lord

excerpts.explanation: Gratitude is carried back to Naam itself here. Thanksgiving becomes deeper than optimism when it is rooted in the One who keeps restoring the heart to remembrance.
